# cast_and_machine
# Baseline of buildCommodityRules — DO NOT hand-edit.
# Regenerate: npx tsx scripts/snapshot-commodity-rules.ts

### context: full
CAST + MACHINE COST INPUT RULES:
  Lines marked deterministic are computed from the measured geometry and will REPLACE whatever you return for them — restate them, do not re-derive them.
  Lines marked UNDECIDED are yours to answer: nothing in the geometry settles them. Answer from the drawing, the photo or the part name, and say which you used.
  leak-tight question=no  [answered — deterministic, use verbatim]
  tolerance-class question=standard  [answered — deterministic, use verbatim]
  safety-critical question=no  [answered — deterministic, use verbatim]
  materialId=mat-lm25  [aluminium gravity casting → LM25 / A356 (A356 / LM25, the heat-treatable gravity / sand alloy — not a drawing callout) — deterministic, use verbatim]
  grade: UNDECIDED — needs "Which aluminium grade?" (EN AC-46200 (AlSi8Cu3, gravity / low-pressure — cylinder heads, housings) | LM4 / AlSi5Cu3 (secondary, sand / gravity) | LM6 / EN AC-44100 (AlSi12, gravity / sand) | LM25 / A356 | EN AC-51300 (AlMg5, marine sand / gravity) | LM13 / EN AC-48000 (AlSi12CuNiMg — pistons) | EN AC-45300 (AlSi5Cu1Mg / C355 — cylinder heads, T6) | A357 / AlSi7Mg0.6 (Premium T6) | A206 / AlCu4.5MgTi (high-strength premium casting))
  subtype=gravity  [gravity: medium-volume aluminium — gravity die casting gives denser, heat-treatable (T6) structure than HPDC for wheels/knuckles/pistons, with cheaper tooling than a pressure die — deterministic, use verbatim]
  yieldFraction=0.6  [gravity aluminium yield band 0.5–0.7, midpoint (feeding scales with the alloy's shrinkage; engineering-typical band, not sourced — the foundry's method yield replaces it) — deterministic, use verbatim]
  netWeightKg=2.8  [1037 cm³ × 0.0027 kg/cm³ (aluminium, confirmed by engineer) — deterministic, use verbatim]
  dieMouldCostGBP=13627  [gravity toolmaker shop model: 194 toolroom hours + steel + bought-outs from a 288 cm² parting footprint, moderate (2 undercut face(s) ≈ 1 slide(s)) — a quotation overrides this — deterministic, use verbatim]
  dieMouldLife=50000  [gravity tool life band 50,000 castings (engineering-typical, not sourced) — deterministic, use verbatim]
  cycleTimeSandGravHr=0.08  [gravity cycle band — deterministic, use verbatim]
  labourId=lab-uk-foundry  [foundry operative on the moulding / die-casting line and at the fettling bench — deterministic, use verbatim]
  fettlingMinutes=2  [light fettling — gravity aluminium, 2.8 kg: gate / riser removal and grind at the foundry rate, 2 min (engineering-typical, not sourced — published manual times run from 45 s a small high-volume ductile casting (Malleable Castings time study) to 15–20 min a cylinder block (Mahindra, 2011)) — deterministic, use verbatim]
  heatTreatCostPerKg=1.1  [gravity aluminium is solution treated and aged, T6 — £1.1/kg × the as-cast kg (advisor rate, UK; engineering-typical, not sourced) — deterministic, use verbatim]
  shotBlastCostPerPart=0.236  [gravity castings are blasted to clean the as-cast surface — oxide and die-joint flash (no sand core is costed on the permanent mould) — 2.85 kg as cast (finished + machining stock) ÷ 600 kg/h (the low end of a 0.5–2 t/h tumble / hanger blast; engineering-typical, not sourced) × (blast machine £25.07/h + operator £24.60/h), min £0.10 = £0.2360 (CostVision engineering heuristic) — deterministic, use verbatim]
  impregnationCostPerPart=0  [not pressure-tight — no impregnation — deterministic, use verbatim]
  impregnation question=no  [not pressure-tight — not asked — deterministic, use verbatim]
  ndtCostPerPart=0  [not safety-critical — no radiography — deterministic, use verbatim]
  manning=1  [one operator to a gravity cell — deterministic, use verbatim]
  leakTestSec=0  [not pressure-tight — no leak test — deterministic, use verbatim]
  ladlePreheatKwhPerT=0  [aluminium — ladle preheat is sourced for iron and steel foundries only (EU JRC SF BREF 2024, BAT-AEPL Tables 4.1 (iron) and 4.2 (steel), kWh per tonne of liquid metal); NOT costed for this metal — deterministic, use verbatim]
  dustExtractionKwhPerT=0  [aluminium — the dust-extraction figure is an iron / steel foundry's (German data restated in the EU JRC SF BREF 2024 §2.3.8.1 (flue-gas cleaning ~20 kWh per tonne of good casting)); NOT costed for this metal — deterministic, use verbatim]
  plantElectricityKwhPerT=0  [gravity aluminium — the plant-electricity figure is a green-sand iron plant's; NOT costed for this route / metal. NOT costed (no published price found): furnace and ladle refractory (8–9 kg/t molten on induction, 1994 data — no current price), the metallurgical lab a melt, the pouring crew beyond the cell crew and the melt shop's operator-hours — deterministic, use verbatim]
  finish question: UNDECIDED — needs "Is the part coated or surface-treated?" (None — bare part | E-coat / KTL (zirconium pre-treat) | Powder coat (iron phosphate pre-treat) | Vibratory mass finish (deburr))
  finishRoute=  [not asked yet — costed bare (answer "Is the part coated?" to price a finish) — deterministic, use verbatim]
  finishAreaM2=0.122  [measured surface 1220.0 cm² = 0.1220 m² — the whole wetted surface; a masked or machined-after-coating face is in it — deterministic, use verbatim]
  castPartWeightKg=2.851  [2.800 kg finished + 18.9 cm³ of 10 hole(s) ≤ 20 mm drilled from solid + 0.0 cm³ machining stock (1.5 mm a side on the machined faces and cored bores, gravity — the total stock a side, assumed (engineering-typical, not sourced): under ISO 8062-3 it is the RMA for the drawing's RMA grade plus half its DCTG casting tolerance, and neither grade is read from a drawing; type the as-cast weight from the drawing or the foundry to override) — deterministic, use verbatim]
  estimatedCycleTimeHr=0.0332  [1.9 min cutting + 0.12 min pallet change (load / unload masked by the cut) (face 0 machined face(s), 0 cm² = 0.0 min (each: 0.2 min positioning + passes × (√area + cutter Ø + 2 × 5 mm clearance) ÷ the table feed n·z·fz — the face taken as √area square, clearance engineering-typical, not sourced); holes 1.8 min (≤ Ø20 drilled from solid, larger cored and finish-bored); 2 tools × 2.2 s (2.2 s chip-to-chip (Okuma MA-4000H 2.15 s ISO 10791-9 / DMG MORI NHX 4000 2.2 s — Okuma MA-4000H brochure (Jul 2025); DMG MORI NHX 4000 2nd generation press release (2016); an HMC figure, no VMC / lathe figure read); positioning / approach / retract allowances engineering-typical, not sourced, not scaled by the metal; sources — aluminium alloy (wrought 6xxx / cast Al-Si rows): face milling vc 1000 m/min, fz 0.2 — Tungaloy TungAlu-Mill standard cutting conditions (2020) (cutter Ø chosen from the face width; teeth Ø50 z4 / Ø63 z5 / Ø100 z6 from the TungAlu-Mill worked table); drilling n·f at Ø12 (n 2600, f 0.31) and Ø16 (n 1900, f 0.33) — Mitsubishi Materials MVE solid carbide drill, recommended cutting conditions (2023); boring vc 400 m/min, f 0.2 mm/rev — Mitsubishi Materials SVJD external turning tool, recommended cutting conditions (2023) (no boring row read for aluminium: the SVJD turning vc, f 0.2 as the Tungaloy T515 boring example); tapping 15 m/min — OSG A-Tap flier n_102, tapping speed chart (2026) (AC / ADC has no advisable band, only "possible" 5–50 m/min — 15 m/min taken inside it; pitch ISO 261 coarse); cutting speeds and feeds from the makers' published recommendations (sources named); cutter bodies, side-pass depth, clearances, allowances and the air-move share are labelled assumptions — not a measured cycle)) — deterministic, use verbatim]
  setupCount=1  [1 fixturing(s) of the volume-cell routing (3 approach direction(s) measured) — deterministic, use verbatim]
  setupTimeHr=0.75  [1 fixturing(s) of the volume-cell routing × 45 min change-over (fixture swap, tool offsets, first-off inspection) a batch (45 min engineering-typical, not sourced) — deterministic, use verbatim]
  batchSize=5000  [100,000/yr ÷ 20 runs a year, held between 50 and 5,000 — deterministic, use verbatim]
  machineId=mach-hmc-400  [cost-ranked 3 routing(s), machine + operator: volume-cell £0.94 (machine £0.50 + operator £0.44; twin-pallet HMC cell at 100,000/yr: 3 direction(s) in 1 clamping(s) on a 4th-axis tombstone, dedicated hydraulic fixture: Horizontal machining centre — 400 mm twin pallet, 4th axis (production cell) £15.11/hr, 1 setup(s) × 45 min / batch 5000 + 7.1 s pallet change per part per fixturing (Okuma MA-4000H 7.1 s, ISO 10791-9 — Okuma MA-4000H brochure (Jul 2025)), 0.6 min load / unload masked by the cut) vs consolidated-5axis £1.42 (machine £0.71 + operator £0.72; single-setup 5-axis consolidation: HAAS UMC-500 (5-axis Mill) £17.07/hr, 1 setup(s) × 45 min / batch 5000 + 0.6 min handling per part per setup) vs split-3axis £2.13 (machine £0.58 + operator £1.55; 3-fixturing split routing: HAAS VF-2 (3-axis Mill) £9.05/hr + CNC Drilling Centre £6.64/hr, 4 setup(s) × 45 min / batch 5000 + 0.6 min handling per part per setup) → volume-cell, £0.48/part cheaper than consolidated-5axis — deterministic, use verbatim]
  operationCount=6  [6 operation(s): cutting by approach direction, 1 measured drilling op, handling and the bench deburr — deterministic, use verbatim]
  operations=Finish machining — +Z side 0.001 hr on mach-hmc-400; Finish machining — -Z side 0.000 hr on mach-hmc-400; Finish machining — +X side 0.000 hr on mach-hmc-400; Drilling — 10 holes (10×Ø10.0×24) [geometry-measured] 0.030 hr on mach-hmc-400; Pallet change — 1 fixturing(s) 0.002 hr on mach-hmc-400; Deburr and gauge check (bench) 0.017 hr on mach-hmc-400  [sums to 0.051 hr: measured cutting, handling per fixturing, bench deburr — deterministic, use verbatim]
  fixtureCostGBP=12000  [1 fixture set(s), one a machine — on the Horizontal machining centre — 400 mm twin pallet, 4th axis (production cell): cycle ÷ OEE 2.4900 min + change-over 0.0090 min = 2.4990 min a part; 2.4990 × 100,000 a year ÷ 60 = 4,165 h; 4,165 h ÷ 6,000 h available = 0.69 machine(s), rounded up — the capacity at this volume; 1 dedicated hydraulic (tombstone) fixture(s) × £12,000 (the volume cell's dedicated fixture; fixture prices engineering-typical toolroom builds, not sourced) — deterministic, use verbatim]
  programmingNRE=58  [CAM programming and prove-out 1.75 h (1.5 h × 1 fixturing(s) + 0.25 h × 1 machined feature group(s)) × £33.27/h manufacturing engineer (hours engineering-typical, not sourced) — deterministic, use verbatim]
  toolWearCostPerPart=0.0749  [1.9 min of cutting × £0.0400/min inserts, end mills and drills (aluminium) — not in the machine rate (£/min engineering-typical, not sourced) — deterministic, use verbatim]
